latin: Herculis ritu modo dictus, o plebs,
english: In Hercules' manner lately said, O people,
note: ritu: after the manner of; dictus: reported

english: to have sought the laurel purchasable by death,
Caesar, the Spanish—, seeks again the Penates,
note: Hispana agrees with ora on line 4

english: victor, from the shore.
The woman rejoicing in her one husband
note: her supplied; mulier = Livia

english: let come forth, having performed the due rites,

latin: et soror clari ducis et decorae
english: and the sister of the famous leader and, adorned
note: decorae (nom. pl.) agrees with matres on line 9

english: with a suppliant fillet,
mothers of maidens and of young men lately

latin: sospitum; vos, o pueri et puellae
english: safe; you, O boys and girls
now experienced of a man, from ill-omened
note: nominatis agrees with verbis on line 12

english: words refrain.

latin: hic dies vere mihi festus atras
english: This day, truly festal for me, black
note: atras agrees with curas on line 14

english: cares will drive out; I neither tumult

latin: nec mori per vim metuam tenente
english: nor to die by violence shall fear, while holding
Caesar the lands.

latin: i pete unguentum, puer, et coronas
english: Go, fetch unguent, boy, and garlands
and a jar mindful of the Marsian war,
if any, Spartacus wandering, could
note: siqua testa: if any jar could escape wandering Spartacus

english: escape, a jar.
Say also that clear-voiced Neaera hasten
note: dic ... properet: tell her to hasten

english: to bind in a knot her myrrh-scented hair;
note: her supplied

english: if through the hateful doorkeeper a delay
shall arise, go away.
Whitening hair softens spirits
desirous of quarrels and of wanton brawling;

latin: non ego hoc ferrem calidus iuventa
english: not would I have borne this, hot with youth,
Plancus being consul.
Wife of poor Ibycus,
at last set a limit to your wickedness
and to your notorious labours;
note: your supplied (tuae on line 2 goes with nequitiae)

english: nearer to a ripe funeral, cease
to play among maidens
and to scatter a cloud over the bright stars.
Not, if anything Pholoe, enough
note: non si quid Pholoen decet, et te satis decet: what befits Pholoe does not therefore befit you

latin: et te, Chlori, decet: filia rectius
english: also you, Chloris, befits: the daughter more rightly
storms the houses of young men,
like a Thyiad stirred by the beaten drum.
Her the love of Nothus compels
to play like a wanton she-goat;
you, wool, near noble
note: lanae tonsae prope nobilem Luceriam: wool shorn near noble Luceria

english: Luceria shorn befit, not lyres,
nor the purple flower of the rose

latin: nec poti, vetulam, faece tenus cadi.
english: nor jars drunk, old woman, down to the dregs.
Shut-in Danae a tower of bronze
and oaken doors and of watchful dogs
the grim night-watches had fortified enough
from nocturnal adulterers,
if not at Acrisius, of the hidden maiden
the fearful guardian, Jupiter and Venus

latin: risissent: fore enim tutum iter et patens
english: had laughed: for that the way would be safe and open
with the god turned into a price.
note: pretium: payment, the shower of gold

english: Gold to go through the midst of guards
and to break through rocks loves, more powerfully
than a lightning stroke: fell the augur's
note: concidit domus auguris Argivi (Amphiaraus)

english: Argive house on account of gain,
sunk in destruction; split cities'
note: diffidit urbium portas: Philip of Macedon

latin: portas vir Macedo et subruit aemulos
english: gates the Macedonian man, and undermined rival
kings with gifts; gifts of ships'
fierce commanders ensnare.
Growing money care follows
and hunger for more. Rightly I have shuddered
to raise a head widely conspicuous,
note: verticem: head, metaphor for prominence

english: Maecenas, ornament of the knights.
By how much each shall have denied himself more,

latin: ab dis plura feret nil cupientium
english: the more from the gods he will bear; of those desiring nothing
note: nil cupientium castra: the camp of those who desire nothing (line 23)

latin: nudus castra peto et transfuga divitum
english: naked I seek the camp, and a deserter of the rich
the party I long to leave,
a more splendid master of a despised property,

latin: quam si quidquid arat inpiger Apulus
english: than if whatever the tireless Apulian ploughs
I were said to hide in my granaries,
among great wealth, poor.
Streams of pure water and a wood of acres

latin: paucorum et segetis certa fides meae
english: few, and the sure faith of my crop
note: paucorum (gen.) with iugerum on line 29

english: him shining with the rule of fertile Africa
escape, a lot more blessed.
note: fallit sorte beatior: my lot, more blessed, escapes his notice

latin: quamquam nec Calabrae mella ferunt apes
english: Although neither do Calabrian bees bring honey,
nor in a Laestrygonian amphora Bacchus
grows mellow for me, nor rich in Gallic
pastures do fleeces grow:
yet importunate poverty is absent,

latin: nec, si plura velim, tu dare deneges.
english: nor, if I should want more, would you refuse to give.
With desire contracted, better my small
note: my supplied

english: revenues shall I stretch
than if the kingdom of Alyattes to the Mygdonian
plains I should join. To those seeking much

latin: desunt multa: bene est cui deus obtulit
english: much is lacking: it is well for him to whom the god has offered
with a sparing hand what is enough.
Aelius, noble from ancient Lamus,

latin: quando et priores hinc Lamias ferunt
english: since both the earlier Lamiae from him they say
were named, and of the descendants
through the recording annals the whole race,
from that founder you draw origin,
who the walls of Formiae is said
as first, and the Liris floating on Marica's
note: innantem Maricae litoribus Lirim: the Liris flowing over Marica's shores

english: shores to have held,
a widely-ruling tyrant:— tomorrow with leaves the grove
many, and the shore with useless seaweed
a storm sent down from Eurus
will strew, unless the augur of water deceives,
the aged crow. While you can, dry
wood lay up: tomorrow your Genius with unmixed wine
note: your supplied

english: you will tend, and with a two-month-old pig,
with the slaves released from tasks.
Faunus, lover of the fleeing Nymphs,

latin: per meos finis et aprica rura
english: through my borders and sunny fields
gently may you walk, and may you go away, to the small
nurslings kindly,

latin: si tener pleno cadit haedus anno
english: if a tender kid falls at the full year
note: cadit: falls as a sacrifice

english: nor are plentiful ones lacking to Venus's companion
note: larga ... vina (line 7); sodali craterae: the mixing-bowl, companion of Venus

english: wines, the mixing-bowl, the old altar with much
fragrance smokes.
Plays on the grassy plain the whole flock
when for you the Nones of December return,
festal, in the meadows, is at leisure with the idle
ox, the village,
among bold lambs the wolf wanders,
the rustic wood scatters leaves for you,
the ditcher rejoices to have struck the hated
earth three times with his foot.
note: his supplied

english: How far distant from Inachus

latin: Codrus pro patria non timidus mori
english: Codrus, not timid to die for the fatherland,
you narrate, and the race of Aeacus

latin: et pugnata sacro bella sub Ilio:
english: and the wars fought under sacred Ilium:
at what price a Chian jar
we may buy, who may temper the water with fires,
who providing the house, and at what hour
I may be free from Paelignian colds, you are silent.
Give, quickly, of the new moon,
note: a cup for the new moon

latin: da noctis mediae, da, puer, auguris
english: give of midnight, give, boy, of the augur
Murena: with three or nine
fitting ladles are the cups mixed.
He who loves the odd-numbered Muses,
three times three ladles, thunderstruck, will ask for,
the bard; beyond three forbids
fearing brawls, to touch, the Grace
note: Gratia prohibet tangere supra tris: the Grace forbids touching more than three

english: joined with her naked sisters.
note: her supplied

english: To rave is pleasing: why of the Berecyntian
pipe do the blasts cease?

latin: cur pendet tacita fistula cum lyra?
english: why hangs the reed-pipe with the silent lyre?
Sparing right hands I
hate: scatter roses, let envious hear
the mad din, Lycus,

latin: et vicina seni non habilis Lyco.
english: and the neighbour woman not suited to old Lycus.
You, glossy with thick hair,
you, like the pure evening star, Telephus,
ripe Rhode seeks;

latin: me lentus Glycerae torret amor meae.
english: me the slow love of my Glycera scorches.
Do you not see with how great danger you move,
Pyrrhus, the cubs of a Gaetulian lioness?
After a little you will flee the hard, un-bold
note: inaudax: cowardly, with raptor on line 4

english: battles, robber,
when through the opposing bands of young men
she will go, seeking again distinguished Nearchus:
a great contest, whether to you the prey should fall
or she the greater.
note: maior an illa: or whether she is the greater (and keeps it)

english: Meanwhile, while you the swift arrows
draw out, she sharpens her teeth to be feared,
note: her supplied

english: the arbiter of the fight to have placed under his bare
note: his supplied; arbiter = Nearchus

english: foot the palm
is said, and to refresh in the gentle wind
his shoulder strewn with scented hair,
note: his supplied

latin: qualis aut Nireus fuit aut aquosa
english: such as either Nireus was, or from watery
Ida the one snatched.
note: Ganymede

english: O born with me, Manlius being consul,

latin: seu tu querellas sive geris iocos
english: whether you bear complaints or jokes
or a brawl and mad loves
or easy sleep, faithful jar,
under whatever name the chosen Massic
you keep, worthy to be moved on a good day,
come down, Corvinus bidding
to bring out mellower wines.
Not he, although he is soaked in Socratic
discourses, neglects you, rough man:
it is related that even of old Cato
the virtue often grew warm with unmixed wine.
You apply a gentle torture to a disposition
generally hard; you of the wise
the cares and the secret, with jesting
counsel uncover, with Lyaeus,
note: iocoso Lyaeo: with jesting Lyaeus (Bacchus, wine)

english: you bring back hope to anxious minds
and strength, and you add horns to the poor man
note: cornua: horns, confidence

english: after you trembling neither at the angry
note: post te: after you (wine) has been drunk

english: crowns of kings nor at soldiers' arms.

latin: te Liber et si laeta aderit Venus
english: You Liber, and Venus, if she shall be present joyful,
and the Graces slow to loosen their knot
note: their supplied

english: and the living lamps will prolong,
until Phoebus, returning, puts the stars to flight.
Guardian of mountains and of groves, maiden,
who girls labouring in the womb
thrice called hear, and take from death,
three-formed goddess,
let the pine overhanging the villa be yours,

latin: quam per exactos ego laetus annos
english: which through the completed years I, glad,
of a boar practising a sidelong stroke
with the blood may present.
If to the sky you shall have raised upturned hands
at the moon's birth, rustic Phidyle,
if with incense you shall have appeased, and with this year's
grain the Lares, and with a greedy sow:
neither will feel the pestilent Africus
the fruitful vine, nor the crop the barren
mildew, or the sweet nurslings
the heavy season in the fruit-bearing year.
For which on snowy Algidus is pastured
note: quae ... victima (line 12)

english: vowed, among oaks and holm-oaks,
or grows in Alban grasses,
the victim, the pontiffs' axes
with its neck will stain: nothing concerns you
note: its supplied

english: to tempt with much slaughter of two-year-old sheep,
the small ones, crowning, with sea-
note: parvos deos coronantem marino rore: crowning the small gods with rosemary (sea-dew)

english: dew the gods and with fragile myrtle.
If a hand free of offering has touched the altar,
note: inmunis: bringing no gift

english: not more winning with a costly victim,
it has softened the averted Penates
with pious spelt and leaping grain.
note: saliente mica: the crackling grain of salt
